summary: Unexpected GPU locking by background metrics collector causing sustained dedicated throughput degradation
description: Issue summary: BrightVoice reported a sustained drop in P50/P95 throughput on their Dedicated pool beginning ~2026-03-10 09:20 UTC. Impact: customer experiences 30-60% lower completed requests per second for batched generation routes, increased request queueing, and occasional 504s. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated tenant) in us-east; running redwood-instruct-3b as primary pinned model. Observed behavior: batcher latencies climb gradually, followed by autoscaler scale-up attempts and then a cascade of short-lived evictions. We observed GPU scheduling stalls concurrent with high-frequency metrics snapshots from a background collector sidecar. Expected behavior: background telemetry should be asynchronous and not hold GPU resources while host inference is running.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route synthetic batched traffic at the same QPS/mean request size as BrightVoice into their dedicated pool (prod us-east).
2) Enable the metrics sidecar with the same collection interval and full-kernel snapshot enabled (metrics-collector v1.4.2 config: snapshot_gpu=on, interval_ms=200).
3) Observe batcher/prefetch timing and GPU utilization over ~10 minutes.
4) Compare with same load but with collector snapshot_gpu=off to confirm regression disappears.
logs: [2026-03-10T09:23:15Z] serving-runtime INFO batcher: batch assembled size=8 latency=120ms
[2026-03-10T09:23:15Z] metrics-collector DEBUG acquiring_gpu_lock for snapshot (tenant=brightvoice, pool=dedicated-us-east)
[2026-03-10T09:23:16Z] batcher ERROR inference_timeout waiting_for_gpu after=300ms route=/generate
[2026-03-10T09:24:00Z] autoscaler INFO scale_up_triggered reason=queue_depth_threshold current_replicas=12 target=18
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: a background telemetry process is synchronously acquiring a GPU resource or pinning the NVMe/GPU DMA path when taking full-kernel snapshots, blocking inference kernels for short windows and triggering cascading scheduling/backpressure effects.
Telemetry: high-frequency (200ms) snapshot configuration observed in customer deployment; collector binary is metrics-collector v1.4.2 (not yet hardened for dedicated pools).
Correlation: GPU lock events in serving logs align with batcher timeouts and immediate autoscaler scale-ups. When snapshots are disabled, throughput returns to baseline in lab repros.

Side-effects: autoscaler reacts to transient queue growth by adding replicas; because collector holds GPU briefly but repeatedly, added replicas experience identical behavior (eviction loops), causing oscillation and effective throughput loss.
Repro steps validated in staging with an instrumented sidecar; root cause narrowed to synchronous cudaMemcopy/trace capture in metrics-collector native shim.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported sustained throughput drop at 09:20 UTC and provided sample logs and collector config. Assigned to infra on-call.
Diego Morales (Infra): Reproduced locally with collector snapshot enabled. Observed gpu_lock traces matching customer logs. Marking as P1 and Sev1 due to dedicated customer impact.

SRE (Lina Chen): Temporary mitigation: advising customer to set metrics-collector.snapshot_gpu=false and increase interval to 10s. Workaround reduced the lock frequency and restored throughput to baseline.

Eng (Ravi Iyer): Created internal issue INT-4182 to patch metrics-collector to use async GPU snapshots and fall back to lightweight telemetry for dedicated pools. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/metrics-collector/pull/214
Customer (BrightVoice - PM): Confirmed temporary workaround applied and throughput restored; requests permanent remediation and release timeline.
resolution: Investigating. Temporary mitigation recommended: set metrics-collector.snapshot_gpu=false and interval >= 10000 ms. Engineering working on async snapshot patch for metrics-collector (see linked PR).
